name: Mibolerone (Cheque Drops)
lead: Mibolerone, also called dimethylnortestosterone (DMNT) and sold under the brand names Cheque Drops and Matenon, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from nandrolone. It was marketed by the Upjohn Company as a veterinary drug to suppress estrus (heat) in adult female dogs.[1][2] Wikipedia describes it as an extremely potent androgen, and it is not approved for human use.[1]

In bodybuilding and strength-sport circles it is discussed as a very potent oral androgen taken shortly before training, with users describing acute increases in strength, aggression and drive.[2][11] The chain that proponents describe is androgen receptor activation, then a stronger training session, then more muscle over time; community commenters themselves dispute whether short-acting use could produce visible growth.[11] In laboratory science, mibolerone is used as a high-affinity androgen receptor ligand in studies of prostate and breast cancer cell lines.[3][4][9]

No published clinical trial has tested mibolerone in humans for muscle gain, appearance or any other purpose. Published animal studies come from veterinary work in dogs, mainly Beagles, and its human-related research is receptor binding and cell-line work.[5][6][7] It is a controlled substance in several countries (Schedule III in the United States, Schedule IV in Canada) and prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency.[1][2]

paras: Mibolerone was approved as an oral veterinary product to prevent estrus in adult female dogs. It acts by inhibiting release of luteinizing hormone from the pituitary, which suppresses ovulation [2]. Dogs typically go into heat about twice a year, with estrus lasting roughly 4 to 13 days, and ovulation follows the luteinizing hormone peak by 24 to 48 hours, so suppressing that peak is the basis of heat suppression [14]. Experimental use in cats has also been reported [2]. The drug is reported to be no longer commercially available in the United States, with supply limited to compounding pharmacies [2].

Labeled contraindications include pregnancy, lactation, prepubertal animals and impaired liver function. Reported adverse effects in dogs include enlargement of the clitoris, vaginitis and vaginal discharge, and increased sebaceous gland activity [2].

A 1980 review of chemotherapeutic oestrus control in the bitch gave particular attention to mibolerone as a recently introduced product.[5] A 1977 evaluation in female Beagles reported that mibolerone effectively inhibited estrous activity in immature and mature animals dosed daily for up to 730 days, with vaginal discharge and a dose-related increase in clitoral size among its effects.[7] A controlled, blind-labelled field trial in 63 bitches across three oral dose levels, with 17 placebo controls, evaluated mibolerone for pseudopregnancy (false pregnancy) and reported significant differences in improvement of clinical signs among dose levels.[6]

Mibolerone is a synthetic estrane steroid and the 17-alpha-methyl derivative of trestolone (7-alpha-methyl-19-nortestosterone, MENT). Its formula is C20H30O2 [1]. Wikipedia describes several preparation routes, including the original patented method starting from nandrolone acetate and a revised route published in 2007 [1]. Related compounds include metribolone and dimethyltrienolone [1].

The 17-alpha methyl group is what makes oral administration possible, and 17-alpha-alkylated steroids as a class are the ones associated with liver effects such as raised liver enzymes, peliosis hepatis and liver tumours in the anabolic steroid literature [12].

Mibolerone binds the androgen receptor with very high affinity and also retains progestogenic activity through the progesterone receptor [1][2]. Wikipedia reports that one comparison found higher androgen receptor affinity and selectivity than metribolone, while a second study found similar progesterone receptor affinity but about half the androgen receptor affinity. In its relative-affinity table, with testosterone at 100 percent, mibolerone scores about 108 percent for the androgen receptor and 214 percent for the progesterone receptor [1].

In research, it has been used as a radioligand-style tool to characterise androgen receptors in human prostate tissue [2], and in androgen-responsive cell lines it alters expression of prostate-specific antigen [2]. A study of breast cancer cell lines used it as a non-metabolizable androgen and found both proliferative and anti-proliferative responses depending on the cell line [4].

A 1985 study of cytosol and nuclear extracts from benign hypertrophic human prostate found that mibolerone binding to the androgen receptor was single-site and of high affinity, compared against the synthetic androgen R1881, and that it did not bind testosterone-binding globulin.[9] Because it is not metabolised like testosterone, researchers use it as a stable probe of androgen signalling, including in studies of prostate-specific antigen regulation in LNCaP cells.[10][2]

Metribolone (R1881), a close relative, became a standard radioligand for androgen receptor assays by the mid-1970s, and Wikipedia notes that its development for advanced breast cancer was abandoned because of liver toxicity at very low doses.[13] Mibolerone fills a similar laboratory role as a stable androgen that is not metabolised like testosterone.[9][10]

No studies found in humans. Related research is veterinary and laboratory work: field and safety trials in dogs and Beagles,[5][6][7][8] receptor binding in human prostate tissue,[9] and cell-line studies in prostate and breast cancer models.[3][4][10]

The Beagle conception study examined effects on conception, pregnancy, parturition and offspring after mibolerone treatment.[8] The 1977 Beagle evaluation reported that pups born to bitches conceiving after mibolerone treatment were grossly normal, and that a decrease in post-treatment conception rate was observed only at the lowest tested daily dose given for 730 days.[7]

Mibolerone was first synthesized in 1963, and Upjohn patents from 1962 and 1967 cover its preparation.[1] It was developed and marketed as a veterinary estrus suppressant, and a 1977 evaluation in female Beagles and a 1980 review of chemotherapeutic oestrus control describe it as a newly introduced product of that period.[5][7] It never received a human indication, and Wikipedia lists no ATC code for it.[1]

According to descriptions of illicit use, mibolerone is taken in bodybuilding and strength circles as an oral pre-training agent, with users reporting short-lived effects on aggression, focus and strength.[2] A looksmax.org thread describes it as stronger than other oral steroids such as Superdrol and Anadrol and nicknames it "hulk juice", while a reply argues its half-life is too short for visible muscle growth at safe doses.[11] Because of the veterinary origin, products circulating outside regulated channels are of uncertain provenance.

subs.h: Related compounds in the same culture
paras: Forum comparisons place mibolerone alongside other potent oral androgens such as Superdrol and Anadrol, and the looksmax.org poster who started the thread names those two as the compounds it is said to exceed.[11] Metribolone, described by Wikipedia as one of the most potent anabolic steroids ever synthesised in rats but never approved for humans, is its closest chemical relative, and the article notes that such potency has not been seen in human studies.[13]

Mibolerone is listed as a controlled substance in the United States (Schedule III), Canada (Schedule IV) and Brazil (Class C5) [1]. WADA prohibits it as an anabolic agent, and anti-doping laboratories detect its metabolites in urine [2].

Adverse effects have been documented in animals, including virilisation of females, reproductive effects and liver changes [2]. For humans, risks are discussed by analogy to other 17-alkylated oral androgens. Wikipedia's anabolic steroid article describes liver effects that are mostly or exclusively linked to 17-alpha-alkylated agents, raised LDL and lowered HDL cholesterol, suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis with testicular atrophy and reduced sperm production, and virilisation in women including voice deepening and clitoral enlargement [12]. No human safety data specific to mibolerone have been published.

Where anabolic steroids are controlled, Wikipedia notes that a black market exists selling smuggled, clandestinely made or counterfeit products, and products circulating outside regulated channels are of uncertain provenance.[12] Anabolic steroids have for many years been among the substances most frequently detected in anti-doping laboratories.[12]

lore.intro: In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums, mibolerone is discussed as an exotic, extremely potent oral androgen of veterinary origin, often in the context of pre-workout aggression and strength.[2][11]

claims.claim: Cheque Drops are the strongest oral steroid for strength and aggression.
claims.believers: Proponents point to its very high androgen receptor affinity and describe sharp strength and drive increases in short bursts before lifting or competition [2]. A looksmax.org poster calls it stronger than every other oral steroid, citing its androgen receptor affinity.[11]
claims.experts: Its receptor binding is documented in laboratory work, but no published human trial has measured strength or behavioural effects [2][3].

claims.claim: Its short action makes it useful as a pre-workout "on demand" compound.
claims.believers: Users say small oral amounts shortly before training give acute mental and performance effects [2]. A thread reply on the same forum questions whether a short half-life could produce visual growth.[11]
claims.experts: No pharmacokinetic or performance studies in humans are available. The only dosing and effect data are from dogs and cats in veterinary studies.[6][7]

claims.claim: It can be used without the downsides of other oral steroids.
claims.believers: Some users argue the very small quantities involved limit side effects.
claims.experts: Veterinary labelling documents virilisation and liver changes in animals, and anabolic steroids in general carry documented risks; human data for mibolerone are absent [2].

claims.claim: It is a hyper-potent relative of other potent oral steroids
claims.believers: A looksmax.org poster calls it stronger than other oral steroids and nicknames it 'hulk juice'.[11]
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes mibolerone as extremely potent and reports very high androgen receptor affinity, while noting that the closely related metribolone's rat potency has not been seen in human studies.[1][13]

claims.claim: A veterinary origin makes it a legitimate pharmaceutical
claims.believers: Posters note that it was a real Upjohn product with a known brand name, Cheque Drops.[1][11]
claims.experts: It was approved only for estrus suppression in female dogs and is a controlled substance in the United States, Canada and Brazil.[1][2]

card.summary: A veterinary oral steroid for dogs that circulates in bodybuilding circles as a hyper-potent pre-workout; no human trials exist.
card.note: Controlled substance in several countries; never studied in humans for appearance or performance.

quick.overview:
Mibolerone is a synthetic androgen that Upjohn sold as Cheque Drops to stop female dogs coming into heat. It is not approved for people.

In bodybuilding circles it is described as an extremely potent oral steroid taken for short-term strength and aggression. Those claims come from community reports; no human studies back them.
quick.mechanism: It binds the androgen receptor very tightly, and also the progesterone receptor. Its 17-alkyl group makes it active when swallowed. In dogs it suppresses luteinizing hormone release, which blocks ovulation.
quick.risks: Animal use is linked to enlarged clitoris, vaginitis and liver changes. Human risks are inferred from other oral steroids, since no human safety data exist. It is controlled in the US, Canada and Brazil and banned in sport.

chain: Binds the androgen receptor with very high affinity
Users report acute strength and drive before training
More muscle and a larger physique over time (claimed)
angle.text: In lifting communities, mibolerone is described as a pre-workout androgen used in short bursts to push strength and aggression for training sessions or meets. Whether this translates into visible muscle is disputed even within those communities, and no human trials exist.
